name: Northwest Buttress
descent_text: The route tops out via a short hand crack onto the upper mountain, then 3rd/4th class scrambling to a sub-summit and the main summit, joining the upper Corkscrew line. From there, descent follows the same terrain used by parties finishing the Southwest Face routes: down the SE Shelf/Corkscrew ledge system. Per a documented Bedal Basin–to–Corkscrew descent account, this involves one roped pitch of low 5th-class downclimbing to gain the main ledge system, then one rappel off the end of the SE Shelf back down to the glacier snowfield; parties descending closer to the true summit sometimes need an additional rappel off a ledge system roughly 400–500 ft below the top before joining that shelf. Once back on the glacier, rope up for crevasse hazard, cross to the 5,800 ft saddle area, and reverse the approach back through the meadow, forest, and washout to the trailhead.
